transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

From what you have described, the most likely cause is clear the air path / vent hose (and condenser on condensers). Check the vent hose out of the back: it should be short, without kinks or squashed sections, and clear of fluff all the way to the outside vent. Was it kinked, squashed or blocked (and is it sorted), or was it already clear?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
yeah just checked, hose is crushed behind the dryer, i pushed it back further recently. theres fluff in the folds too. also the dryer gets really hot before it stops

That fits clear the air path / vent hose (and condenser on condensers). Once that is sorted, run it again: does it work normally now?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok how do i sort it? just straighten the hose out and clean the fluff? its my landlords dryer so dont wanna break it

Yes. With the dryer unplugged, pull it forward, straighten the hose, clear the fluff out of it and the outlet, and clean the lint filter, then push the dryer back without kinking the hose. That fits clear the air path / vent hose (and condenser on condensers). Once that is sorted, run it again: does it work normally now?
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
